1.explanation:
1. Prepare a base trace file (e.g. from Chrome DevTools > Record > Save as JSON or from Lighthouse `--save-assets`).
2. Put that JSON at `trace.json` next to the script.
3. Adjust the `metrics` array in the script to use your real measured times (in ms).
4. Run `node injectMetrics.js`. This will append 'mark' events (phase 'R') at the right timestamps.
5. Open Chrome and go to chrome://tracing or DevTools > Performance (Timeline) tab and load `trace-with-metrics.json`.
   You should now see thin vertical markers labeled with each Lighthouse metric exactly where they occur on the timeline, reproducing the bug scenario shown in the screenshot.
1.bug_scenario: In the Timeline pane of DevTools you should see your standard Chrome tracing bars (Main, GPU, network, etc.), but with extra “marker‐style” annotations for each Lighthouse metric (First Contentful Paint, First Meaningful Paint, First Visual Change, Visually Complete, Perceptual Speed Index, Time to Interactive). In the provided screenshot you can see thick colored bars under the “Interactions” lane instead of thin vertical markers at the exact timestamp of each metric. This demonstrates the fake trace events were injected but are being rendered as long slices rather than point markers.
